record.paper_title: Dense ideals in topological algebras: some results and open problems
record.original_question: Let A be a commutative unital complex m-convex B0-algebra, meaning a completely metrizable locally convex algebra whose topology can be given by a sequence of submultiplicative seminorms. Must every multiplicative linear functional on A be continuous? Equivalently, must every codimension-one maximal ideal of A be closed?

evidence.quote: Unless otherwise stated, all algebras in this paper will be commutative, complex, unital, with the unity denoted by e.
– The class MB0 = MLC ∩ F of all m-convex B0-algebras, where the relations (4) are replaced by (2).

Problem 1. Let A be a commutative unital m-convex B0-algebra. Is it true that all its multiplicative-linear functionals are continuous ? In other words: is it true that all maximal ideals of A of codimension one are closed ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let A be a commutative, unital, complex topological algebra that is an m-convex B_0-algebra; that is, A is a completely metrizable locally convex topological vector space whose topology can be defined by a countable family of seminorms (p_n)_{n≥1} satisfying p_n(xy) ≤ p_n(x) p_n(y) for all x, y ∈ A and all n. (Equivalently, A is a commutative unital Fréchet algebra whose topology is given by a sequence of submultiplicative seminorms.)

Question: Must every multiplicative linear functional φ : A → ℂ be continuous? Equivalently, must every maximal ideal of A of codimension one be closed?
artifact.status_search_result: This is Michael's problem (1952), one of the most famous open problems in the theory of topological algebras. It remains widely regarded as open. Recent work (e.g., Esterle's 2023 paper on Picard–Borel ideals in Fréchet algebras and Michael's problem) treats it as still unresolved. A 2020 arXiv preprint claims an affirmative resolution, but this has not been accepted as a verified solution in the community.

status_evidence.title: Picard–Borel ideals in Fréchet algebras and Michael's problem (Esterle, 2023)
status_evidence.snippet: Dense Picard–Borel ideals could play a role in the construction of discontinuous characters on some commutative unital Fréchet algebras, relevant for Michael's problem.
status_evidence.claim: Treats Michael's problem as still open in 2023.

status_evidence.title: On affirmative solution to Michael's acclaimed problem in the theory of Fréchet algebras (arXiv:2006.11134)
status_evidence.snippet: In 1952, Michael posed a question about the functional continuity of commutative Frechet algebras... The author settles this in the affirmative.
status_evidence.claim: A claimed affirmative solution exists as a preprint but is not generally accepted.
